headlines.title: Richmond officer shot by woman while responding to behavioral health crisis call
headlines.description: A Richmond police officer was seriously injured after being shot while responding to a behavioral health crisis call Thursday evening, police said. Contra Costa County’s behavioral health crisis response team was called to conduct a mental health check on a person in the 2200 block of Key Boulevard shortly after 6:30 p.m. Richmond police were asked to assist because of potential safety concerns, according to authorities. Police said the first officer to arrive at the home was struck by gunfire almost immediately. The officer was taken to a hospital in serious condition but is expected to survive. Following the shooting, a female suspect barricaded herself inside the home and continued firing multiple rounds from within, police said. According to the police chief, bullets struck neighboring homes, cars and a Richmond police patrol vehicle. No residents or additional personnel were injured. Multiple agencies responded to the scene, including SWAT teams, the Contra Costa County Sheriff’s Office and crisis negotiators. Police eventually used chemical agents, and the suspect came out of the home and was taken into custody. The officer was the only person injured during the incident. The investigation remains ongoing.
headlines.source: Victoria Meza and Ginger Conejero Saab

headlines.title: Bicyclist dies after collision in San Jose
headlines.description: A bicyclist was killed in a collision early Friday morning in San Jose, police said. Officers responded at about 4:20 a.m. to the intersection of Trimble Road and North First Street for a collision involving a vehicle and a bicyclist. A preliminary investigation found that a man driving a gray 2024 Toyota Corolla was traveling westbound on Trimble Road through a green light when he struck a bicyclist traveling northbound on North First Street in the crosswalk, according to police. When officers arrived, they found an adult man unconscious and not breathing. He was pronounced dead at the scene, according to police. The driver remained at the scene and cooperated with investigators, according to police. Drugs and alcohol do not appear to have been factors in the collision, police said. The death marks San Jose’s 33rd fatal collision and 33rd traffic-related death of 2026. The investigation remains ongoing.

headlines.title: Caldecott Tunnel to get $267 million in state and federal help with upgrades
headlines.description: State leaders have announced a slew of funding going towards transportation infrastructure across the state, and that includes funding for major upgrades to the East Bay’s Caldecott Tunnel. These changes would fund the ventilation project at the tunnel as well as make improvements to pavement, drainage, and lighting. Gov. Gavin Newsom announced that the state is investing a total of $2.7 billion in more than 150 transportation projects across the state, using $1.6 billion in federal funding and $542 million from state funding. In Newsom’s announcement about these statewide projects, the Caldecott Tunnel was at the top of the list. The update from his office said $267 million of that funding will go towards rehabilitating and upgrading the ventilation systems on three of the four bores at the Caldecott Tunnel. The announcement says this project will replace the tunnel’s structural pavement, upgrade drainage, and improve electrical systems to LED lighting. This provides funding for a ventilation project Caltrans has already been working towards. Caltrans said they do not have a date scheduled yet for when the major work will begin on this project. headlines.title: Stanford community honors late soccer player Katie Meyer
headlines.description: It was a historic and emotional Thursday night at Stanford, as the women’s soccer team retired number 19: the number worn by star goalkeeper Katie Meyer, who died by suicide in 2022. Meyer’s parents, Gina and Steve, walked to midfield to a standing ovation, surrounded by the team, coaches and fans who came to honor their daughter. “It warms my heart, breaks my heart, warms my heart, the whole thing,” Steve Meyer said. “We used to walk in through those doors. I see it in my eyes right now, so it’s tough. She’d be right over there warming up,” Katie Meyer was a captain for Stanford. In the 2019 national championship game, she made two critical saves to help Stanford beat North Carolina. If you or someone you know is in crisis, call or text 988 to reach the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline or chat live at 988lifeline.org. You can also visit SpeakingOfSuicide.com/resources for additional support. headlines.title: Pittsburg officer, suspect shot after altercation during booking process
headlines.description: A police officer and a suspect hospitalized after being shot during an altercation at the Pittsburg police station Thursday, according to the police department. Police said officers arrested a 31-year-old man and took him to the police station for booking. While booking, authorities said a physical altercation occurred between the suspect and an officer, during which a firearm was discharged, striking the officer and the suspect. The officer was taken to John Muir Medical Center in Walnut Creek in serious but stable condition. The suspect was also hospitalized and was in stable condition, according to police. Police have not said whose firearm was discharged or provided additional details about what led up to the struggle. The shooting remains under investigation.

headlines.title: Multiple businesses burglarized in Danville
headlines.description: At least 11 businesses in Danville were burglarized early Tuesday morning, leaving owners on edge. Xu Xia, a worker at Hashiya Sushi, came to work Tuesday morning to find the newly opened sushi restaurant had been burglarized. Surveillance video shows three men dressed in hoodies smashing through the front door and going straight to the cash register which fortunately was nearly empty. The burglars smashed into a neighboring Vietnamese restaurant, also going straight for the cash. In the same shopping center, they smashed their way into a nail salon, also Asian owned. “I think they probably thought they probably thought Asians had more cash in the store,so that’s why they target mostly Asian restaurants,” Xia said. Across the street, three more businesses were hit: a Thai restaurant, a Greek restaurant and another sushi spot. On the other side of town, burglars targeted five more businesses, including a hair salon. Stylist Connie Palomino says, surprisingly, the only thing they took was one of the surveillance cameras and some snacks. She speculates all the break-ins worked up an appetite. The burglars also loaded up with liquor at Los Panchos Mexican Restaurant and tried to break the cash register. Thieves also hit a kebab restaurant, a Domino’s and an Indian eatery. The burglary spree has business owners on edge. Many are asking for more police protection. NBC Bay Area reached out to Danville police but has not heard back.

headlines.title: Morgan Hill summer camp counselor accused of sexually assaulting 10-year-old girls
headlines.description: A Gilroy man accused of sexually assaulting three 10-year-old girls while working as a summer camp counselor is scheduled to be arraigned Friday. Anthony Joseph Ramon faces five counts of felony child molestation for attacks the district attorney claims took place in June at a Morgan Hill swim center. The 25-year-old Ramon was arrested three different times for each alleged assault. Prosecutors not only want him to be held accountable, but also want to know why Ramon was allowed to post bail after each arrest. Santa Clara County District Attorney Jeff Rosen intends to ask the judge to hold Ramon on no bail during Friday’s formal arraignment on multiple assaults. “Bail should always be about protecting public safety,” Rosen said in a statement. “The idea that a person suspected of sexually abusing multiple children should get the same chance at freedom as a person accused of mail fraud or some other non-violent crime is wrong, and dangerous.” Santa Clara County Aug 31 Gilroy Aug 16 Legal analyst Steven Clark said Ramon was allowed to post bail because each arrest occurred separately. “Now that the cases will be consolidated in one place, that’s where I think the court will the say ‘He’s now facing a life sentence and no bail is allowed,'” Clark said. “But for the defense, they’re gonna say that he has made his court appearance that he posted enough bail to secure both his appearances. He’s not a flight risk and he is presumed innocent.” Ramon was a counselor for YMCA Silicon Valley when he worked a school summer camp field trip to the Morgan Hill Aquatic Center. In the weeks following, police arrested Ramon repeatedly after three individual 10-year-old girls came forward — one by one — claiming he molested them in the pool. Police said the case is an active investigation and are still looking for more possible victims.

headlines.title: Musk launches steering-wheel-free taxi service in bet riders lose ‘no control' fears and hop inside
headlines.description: Elon Musk sent dozens of self-driving Cybercabs without steering wheels or brake pedals onto the streets of Austin, Texas, on Thursday, betting that Americans will overcome their fears of rides with “no control” and hop inside. The rollout of the gold-colored Teslas, which give passengers no way to take control in an emergency, comes as the company prepares to launch the service in other cities. Tesla shares have suffered amid a slump in vehicle sales, but they rose more than 5% Thursday on hopes that the futuristic-looking taxis will catch on quickly. “No steering wheel, no pedals,” Tesla teased on X before the launch. Musk followed with a post showing a giant Cybercab floating above the Austin skyline and later wrote, “A Storm of Cybercabs.” An invitation-only launch event was expected to be held later Thursday. It is unclear how soon Musk intends to roll out the Cybercab service, but he needs to move quickly. Tesla trails self-driving taxi leader Waymo in the number of cabs deployed and trips completed. To catch up, it must demonstrate that its camera-only system can safely navigate streets and avoid pedestrians. By contrast, Waymo and another rival, Amazon’s Zoox, supplement cameras with radar and a laser-based technology called lidar. Even if the technology works well, Americans still need to be convinced. A Pew Research Center survey conducted in February found that seven in 10 U.S. adults were “not too” or “not at all” comfortable riding in a driverless car. Tesla stock was battered last year after Musk took over President Donald Trump’s government cost-cutting campaign, dubbed DOGE, and embraced extreme-right political candidates, sparking protests at Tesla showrooms and boycotts by car buyers in several countries. Tesla posted a second consecutive annual decline in vehicle sales last year. Its profits plunged, and it lost its crown as the world’s best-selling electric vehicle maker to China’s BYD. Austin has had a self-driving Tesla “robotaxi” service since June last year, but those cars are equipped with steering wheels and brake pedals. The service, which has since expanded to five other cities in Texas and Florida, initially carried passengers with safety drivers aboard to take over in case of problems. Tesla has more than 200 “unsupervised” robotaxis in those cities, meaning they operate without safety drivers aboard, according to the monitoring site RobotaxiTracker. Waymo has more than 4,000 such vehicles in 14 cities. In the Pew survey, 16% of U.S. adults said they would be “somewhat” comfortable riding in a driverless car, while 7% said they would be “extremely” or “very” comfortable. Separate Gallup polling conducted in 2025 found that skepticism about the safety of driverless cars had risen over the previous several years. More Americans said all or mostly human-operated cars were the safest option than in a 2018 poll. It is unclear whether Musk is the right person to coax people into cars with no human controls. Another Pew poll conducted in January found that nearly six in 10 U.S. adults had a “very” or “mostly” unfavorable view of him. Musk eventually hopes to send full self-driving software to hundreds of thousands of Teslas through a software update. That would allow Tesla owners to turn their cars into taxis for hire when they are not using them. But regulators in the U.S. and overseas have signaled that he still has some convincing to do. Tesla has not received approval for drivers to use even its partial self-driving software in most European Union countries. In the U.S., where the software has been downloaded and used, regulators have opened several investigations into its safety. One probe is examining the software’s role in several Tesla crashes in fog, sun glare and other low-visibility conditions, including one in which a pedestrian was killed. Another is investigating dozens of incidents in which Teslas using partial self-driving software ran red lights or drove on the wrong side of the road, sometimes crashing into other vehicles and causing injuries. A third is examining why Tesla apparently violated regulatory requirements by failing to report crashes promptly.

headlines.title: New Steller sea lion appears at San Francisco's Pier 39
headlines.description: A sizable sea lion appeared at San Francisco’s Pier 39 Thursday, and many wonder if this Steller sea lion is Chonkers or another “sizable star.” “Well, the guy in the middle is like the head honcho. We were just talking about him. He’s like the dude in charge,” Katie, who is visiting from New Jersey, said. This Steller sea lion is more than double the size of the California sea lions that have helped make Pier 39 so popular over the years. Earlier this year Chonkers, a gigantic Steller sea lion, came to Pier 39 and spent weeks there. It didn’t take long for him to become kind of legendary, particularly online. The new sea lion showed up Thursday afternoon at Pier 39, and staff came out to check to see if this is Chonkers. However, they say the new sea lion is a little smaller than Chonkers, so they are not quite sure yet. Chonkers ruled Pier 39 for a few weeks in April and May. His coat was lighter colored than most of the California sea lions around him. Back then, spotters said he also happened to have a smaller Steller sea lion with him. Now, one of the theories is that Chonkers sidekick back then could be the one who showed back up at Pier 39. Nobody’s 100%, but everyone says it’s still a sight to see. Steller sea lions can grow up to 2,500 pounds, while the biggest California sea lion was 1,000 pounds. Seeing one in the state is rare because they usually stick to colder environments like Alaska and don’t usually venture into urban settings. But earlier this year, the harbor master at Pier 39 said the Bay has been teaming with anchovies and other fish to feed on, which is possibly what has been attracting Chonkers and others to the area and “feeding” the big debate over the identity of this super-sized sea lion.

headlines.title: San Francisco supervisor wants to ensure city is ready for Fleet Week crowds
headlines.description: A San Francisco supervisor held a hearing Thursday to make sure the city is prepared for expected massive crowds for Fleet Week. Supervisor Stephen Sherrill said San Francisco underestimated crowds at both a 4th of July celebration and Formula 1 demonstration, which triggered problems and even bigger gridlock in the city. “I heard they are assuming there will be larger crowds and I think that’s a great start,” Sherrill said of the city’s preparation for Fleet Week, which includes 20% more porta potties and 30% more capacity for MTA service. “What I want to make sure happens is that there is real-time coordination to understand if there are any traffic impacts.” The supervisor also said the city is coordinating with rideshare and autonomous vehicle companies to manage where they can and can’t drop off and pick up riders. A public affairs officer for San Francisco Fleet Week said after producing the event for 45 years, they are confident in their planning process and expect another successful celebration. headlines.title: Preliminary 3.3 magnitude earthquake strikes near Santa Rosa
headlines.description: A 3.3 magnitude earthquake struck near Santa Rosa, according to the United States Geological Survey. The quake hit at 10:33 a.m. Thursday and was centered four miles north of the Sonoma County city, the USGS said. The temblor was initially reported as a 3.5 magnitude. This is a developing story. Details may change as more information becomes available. Stay tuned for updates.
